title: HOW DEEP DO LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS INTERNALIZE SCIENTIFIC LITERATURE AND CITATION PRACTICES?

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the median citation counts of existing LLM-generated references to ground-truth human references using pairwise two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests to evaluate the reinforcement of the Matthew effect.
Comparing the distribution of publication years of LLM-generated references against ground-truth references to measure the model's systematic preference for more recently published papers.
Analyzing the distribution of the number of authors in generated references compared to ground-truth references to identify a preference for papers with fewer authors (smaller teams).
Comparing the median number of characters in the titles of generated references versus ground-truth references to measure a preference for shorter, more condensed titles.
Analyzing the frequency distribution of journal venues in generated references compared to ground-truth references to identify an amplified preference for high-impact and prestigious journals.
